rows: A scorpion's median and lateral eyes together look almost all the way around the body, so the picture covers nearly the full circle.
Scorpion eyes peak in the green near 500 to 570 nanometres and have a secondary peak in the ultraviolet, so the picture leans toward green and ultraviolet light.
Scorpion eyes respond to starlight levels of light, so the view keeps a bright picture on a moonless night.

No one has measured how sharp a scorpion's picture is. This view keeps a coarse picture of shapes, with colour limited to green, blue and ultraviolet, and the brightness and fading are the app's choices.
Scorpions sense vibration through slits in their legs and touch through hairs and pegs. Most of what they find comes through these senses, which the picture does not show.

claims.how: Both records state a 360 degree field of view for scorpions, so the value is 360, graded g because the records come from a review and a wider group.
